evidence.title: Wolo Sege & Mata Menge (So'a Basin, Flores): ~1.02–0.70 Ma Wallacean sea crossing & dwarf hominins
evidence.summary: Stone artifacts at Wolo Sege (~1.02 Ma) and diminutive 700 ka Mata Menge mandibles/humerus demonstrate archaic hominins crossed deep Wallacean marine straits long before Homo sapiens.
evidence.limits: Ocean currents or accidental rafting vs intentional watercraft remain unverified for >700 ka crossings.

evidence.title: Liang Bua Cave (Flores): Late Pleistocene Homo floresiensis & 61 ka aridification shift
evidence.summary: Stratigraphic revision confines small-bodied Homo floresiensis skeletal remains to 100–60 ka and stone tools to 190–50 ka amid 61 ka monsoon aridification before modern human arrival.
evidence.limits: Whether H. floresiensis encountered early H. sapiens across Wallacea remains unestablished in stratified beds.

evidence.title: Walanae Basin & Maros–Pangkep Karst (Sulawesi): >1 Ma tools & ≥67.8 ka cave hand stencils
evidence.dateLabel: >1.04 Ma stone tools; ≥67.8–51.2 ka parietal art
evidence.summary: Ancient stone tools in Sulawesi's Walanae Basin prove pre-modern sea crossings alongside the world's oldest dated figurative/stencil rock art (≥67.8 ka) on the gateway to Sahul.
evidence.limits: Hominin taxon responsible for >1.04 Ma Walanae tools remains unknown without skeletal fossils.

evidence.title: Laili, Asitau Kuru (Timor-Leste) & Tron Bon Lei (Alor): 44–20 ka Wallacean pelagic fishing & shell hooks
evidence.dateBasis: Calibrated radiocarbon on marine shell & charcoal
evidence.summary: Deep Wallacean island caves document ~44 ka pelagic tuna fishing, early rotating shell fishhooks, and terminal Pleistocene inter-island obsidian transfers between Alor, Timor, and Kisar.
evidence.limits: Early coastal sites below -120 m LGM shorelines are submerged.

evidence.title: Mololo Cave (Waigeo, Raja Ampat): 55–50 ka Northern Sahul pioneer plant processing
evidence.dateBasis: Calibrated radiocarbon on resin and bone
evidence.summary: On Equatorial Waigeo Island facing Bird's Head New Guinea, Mololo Cave provides the earliest radiocarbon-dated horizon on the Northern Route into Sahul (~55–50 ka).
evidence.limits: Intervening karst erosion limits mid-Pleistocene resolution.

evidence.title: Sahul & Wallacea Deep Genomics: Long-chronology settlement & Denisovan–Sapiens introgression
evidence.dateBasis: Ancient & modern whole-genome Bayesian coalescent modeling
evidence.summary: Papuan and Aboriginal Australian genomes preserve multiple distinct Denisovan admixture pulses and ~50–60 ka divergence supporting early Sahul peopling and long-term regional continuity.
evidence.limits: Exact geographic locations of Denisovan admixture events along Sunda–Wallacea–Sahul remain inferred.

evidence.title: Madjedbebe (NT): 65 ka seed grinding, Pandanus plant food & ground-edge axes
evidence.summary: Macrobotanical Pandanus remains and continuous 65 ka grinding stones establish deep technological and dietary complexity at Australia's oldest excavated rock shelter.
evidence.limits: Sand-apron grain displacement continues to draw debate between 65 ka vs ~50 ka camps.

evidence.title: Lake Mungo & Willandra Claypan Trackways (NSW): 42 ka burials & 20 ka footprints
evidence.summary: Willandra preserves the world's oldest cremation (WLH 1), ochre-sprinkled WLH 3 burial, and >450 fossilized human footprints tracking family movement across an Ice Age claypan.
evidence.limits: Aeolian reactivation and erosion threaten exposed claypan trackways.

evidence.title: Kow Swamp & Keilor (Victoria): Terminal Pleistocene burials & late Pleistocene cranium
evidence.summary: Cemeteries at Kow Swamp (>40 individuals with grave goods and cranial shaping) and the Keilor cranium anchor late Pleistocene–early Holocene diversity in southeastern Australia.
evidence.limits: Repatriation for ceremonial reburial prevents further destructive isotope sampling.

evidence.title: Cuddie Springs & Continental Megafauna Debate: Taphonomy vs coexistence
evidence.summary: Stone tools, grinding stones, and Diprotodon fossils in Cuddie Springs' ephemeral lake focus scientific debate on human–megafauna overlap versus vertical claypan mixing.
evidence.limits: Disputed stratigraphic association without undisturbed primary bone-tool beds.

evidence.title: Dargan Shelter & Cloggs Cave (SE Highlands, NSW/Vic): 25–20 ka cold-montane habitation
evidence.summary: High-elevation LGM occupation at Dargan Shelter (1,073 m) and 25 ka–Holocene Gunaikurnai sequences at Cloggs Cave establish ice-age alpine adaptation in SE Australia.
evidence.limits: Freezing glacial temperatures drove seasonal upland visits rather than winter sedentism.

evidence.title: Koonalda Cave, Wyrie Swamp & Roonka Flat (SA): Subterranean flint, 10 ka boomerangs & cemeteries
evidence.summary: Nullarbor subterranean flint mining at Koonalda (~20 ka), 10.2 ka wooden boomerangs at Wyrie Swamp, and 8,000-year Roonka burials highlight deep South Australian continuity.
evidence.limits: Taphonomic preservation hinges on dry Nullarbor karst or anaerobic peat wetlands.

evidence.title: Boodie Cave, Kimberley Shelters & Gwion Rock Art (WA): 50 ka coast & 16–12 ka art
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon on mud-wasp nests, shell beads & OSL
evidence.summary: Northwest Australian karst shelters document 50 ka marine-shelf adaptation at Boodie Cave and mud-wasp-dated Gwion/Irregular Infill rock art older than 12–16 ka.
evidence.limits: Sea-level rise erased earliest >50 ka Pleistocene coastal camps offshore.

evidence.title: Murujuga / Dampier Archipelago (Pilbara, WA): Over 1 million incised petroglyphs
evidence.summary: More than one million petroglyphs track transitions from extinct terrestrial mammals and climbing figures to sea-level rise and dugong/turtle maritime art.
evidence.limits: Industrial emissions threaten weathering of ancient rock varnish across Burrup slopes.

evidence.title: Lutruwita / Tasmania Ice-Age Caves & Burning: 41.6 ka entry to Kutikina & Kelly Basin
evidence.dateBasis: Lacustrine charcoal cores & limestone cave radiocarbon
evidence.summary: Aboriginal landscape burning appears ~41.6 ka before peak LGM Kutikina/Warreen cave occupation (~35–13 ka) and Holocene coastal *rikawa* kelp-vessel adaptation after Bass Strait flooding.
evidence.limits: Pleistocene Bassian plains are submerged beneath Bass Strait.

evidence.title: Kaakutja & Australian Colonial Frontier Conflicts (1200 CE & 1794–1900)
evidence.dateBasis: Bioarchaeological trauma, cartridge forensics & colonial archives
evidence.summary: Direct skeletal evidence of pre-colonial boomerang trauma near Toorale alongside cartridge/massacre archaeology across NSW, Tasmania, WA, SA, and Queensland reconstructs armed Indigenous defense.
evidence.limits: Biased colonial policing reports require archaeological survey and Aboriginal oral history to corroborate.

evidence.title: Kuk Swamp & Highlands New Guinea (PNG): 10 ka–4.5 ka independent drainage agriculture
evidence.dateLabel: c. 10,000 BP mounds; 4,500 BP ditched plots
evidence.summary: Highland Papuan farmers cultivated taro, bananas, and yam along drained wetland grids in the Wahgi Valley, supporting dense non-Austronesian highlands communities.
evidence.limits: Early pre-4500 BP wetland modification intensity remains scrutinized.

evidence.title: Teouma (Vanuatu), Caution Bay & Koné (New Caledonia): Lapita maritime expansion
evidence.summary: Austronesian voyagers moved across the Bismarcks, Solomons, southern New Guinea, Vanuatu, and New Caledonia within three centuries (~3,100–2,850 BP), carrying pottery and Talasea obsidian.
evidence.limits: Subsequent Papuan admixture rapidly reshaped island gene pools across Remote Melanesia.

evidence.title: Massim Kula Seascape & Roviana Lagoon Fortifications (PNG & Solomon Islands)
evidence.dateBasis: Obsidian XRF, ceramic temper & hillfort survey
evidence.summary: Island Melanesian chiefdoms built fortified coral-stone complexes in Roviana, institutionalized Kula shell exchange in Milne Bay, and fielded long-distance *tomoko* war canoes.
evidence.limits: Direct chronological resolution on open hillfort wall phases remains patchy.

evidence.title: Micronesia Monumental Complexes: Marianas Latte, Palau Earthworks, Nan Madol & Leluh
evidence.dateLabel: c. 1500 BCE settlement; 450 BCE–1850 CE monuments
evidence.dateBasis: U-series coral dating, XRF basalt sourcing & AMS
evidence.summary: From ~1500 BCE Marianas crossings to Babeldaob terraced ridges, Yapese stone money, and coral-basalt capitals at Nan Madol and Leluh, Micronesian architects engineered island landscapes.
evidence.limits: Colonial depopulation curtailed monumental maintenance prior to 1900.

evidence.title: Lapaha (Tonga), Fiji Hillforts (*Koro ni Valu*) & Pulemelei (Samoa): West Polynesian states
evidence.dateBasis: LiDAR earthwork mapping, U-series & XRF geochemistry
evidence.summary: West Polynesia shifted from Nukuleka/Bourewa Lapita villages to monumental *langi* royal tombs, star mounds at Pulemelei, and LiDAR-mapped hillforts/earth forts across Fiji and Tonga.
evidence.limits: Vegetation cover still masks inland fortification trenches in Fiji and Savaiʻi.

evidence.title: Aotearoa New Zealand & Rēkohu: 1280 CE arrival, *pā* forts, Musket Wars & Moriori survival
evidence.dateBasis: High-precision AMS, obsidian network analysis & colonial records
evidence.summary: East Polynesian voyagers settled Aotearoa and Rēkohu (Chathams) c. 1280–1450 CE, built hundreds of fortified *pā*, exchanged obsidian and *pounamu*, and later fought the Musket and New Zealand Wars.
evidence.limits: Marine-reservoir corrections influence early coastal midden chronologies.

evidence.title: Taputapuātea, Rapa Iti, Hawaiʻi & Rapa Nui: Eastern Polynesian voyages & monuments
evidence.dateBasis: Bayesian radiocarbon, XRF quarry sourcing & paleoecology
evidence.summary: From Taputapuātea *marae* on Raʻiatea to Rapa Iti hillforts, Hawaiian *heiau* and Mauna Kea quarries, and Rapa Nui's enduring rock gardens and *moai*, East Polynesians transformed distant oceanic islands.
evidence.limits: Short vs long colonization models converge on c. 1000–1250 CE dispersal across East Polynesia.

evidence.title: Madjedbebe Botanical Assemblage (NT): 65–53 ka Pandanus & tuber processing
evidence.summary: Charred Pandanus shells and underground storage tubers show complex plant-processing technology in tropical Sahul immediately upon arrival.
evidence.limits: Bioturbation around deep sand margins stays closely evaluated.

evidence.title: Nauwalabila I (Arnhem Plateau, NT): 55 ka early Arnhem sequence
evidence.summary: Arnhem Land gorge shelter containing basal hematitic sandstone grindstones and abundant flaking debris.
evidence.limits: Sand-column mixing complicates precision below 45 ka.

evidence.title: Boodie Cave (Barrow Island, WA): 50 ka Pleistocene coast & shell beads
evidence.summary: Preserves Pleistocene coastal shellfish gathering, dugong-shelf hunting, and earliest NW Australian beads prior to sea-level separation.
evidence.limits: Abandoned after island separation ~6.8 ka.

evidence.title: Drysdale / Gunu & Borologa 1 (Kimberley, WA): Dated ochre & Pleistocene art context
evidence.summary: Buried hematite painting residues and mud-wasp nests anchor continuous Kimberley sandstone habitation and figurative art.
evidence.limits: Acidic sand layers preserve mineral pigments better than organic DNA.

evidence.title: Devil's Lair & Greater Swan Plain (SW WA): 48 ka karst beads to Holocene coast
evidence.summary: Karst cave bone beads (~48 ka) linked with SW sand-ridge hunter-gatherer camps through postglacial sea-level rise.
evidence.limits: Offshore plain submerged west of Rottnest Island.

evidence.title: Awunbarna & Maliwawa Galleries (Arnhem Land, NT): Dynamic, Maliwawa & Contact art
evidence.summary: Distinct Maliwawa and blue-pigment panels record macropod hunters alongside historic Moluccan/Macassan contact vessels.
evidence.limits: Stylistic phasing awaits more mineral-crust absolute ages.

evidence.title: Sydney Basin, Parramatta & Bass Point (NSW): 34–20 ka eastern seaboard camps
evidence.summary: Pre-LGM ochre processing at Parramatta and Bass Point / Burrill Lake coastal middens chart continuous eastern seaboard habitation.
evidence.limits: Ridge sandstone weathering obscures age of open engravings.

evidence.title: Baaka–Darling Weirs & Kaakutja (NSW): Holocene fish traps & 1200 CE trauma
evidence.summary: Barkandji stone fish traps and Kaakutja boomerang skeletal trauma demonstrate dense riverine economies and pre-colonial conflict.
evidence.limits: Colonial paddle-steamer traffic removed several mid-river weirs.

evidence.title: Mithaka & Kooroongoora (Channel Country, SW Qld): Gunyah villages & lodges
evidence.summary: Circular stone hut foundations, seed-grinding quarries, and defensive Warrior Lodges mark a dense desert exchange crossroads.
evidence.limits: Surface deflation merges late Holocene occupation horizons.

evidence.title: Warreen Cave & Eastern Lutruwita (Tasmania): 35 ka karst to kelp vessels
evidence.summary: Ice-age wallaby specialization in Southern Forests caves transitioning to Holocene open coastal hunting and *rikawa* kelp containers.
evidence.limits: Open coastal middens suffered heavy sealing-era destruction.

evidence.title: Torres Strait & Jiigurru / Lizard Island (NE Qld): Coral Sea shrines & pottery
evidence.summary: Dugong mounds, *kod* men's shrines, and reef ceramic imports prove dynamic Papuan–Cape York maritime borderlands.
evidence.limits: Tropical storms periodically reworked low cay beach ridges.

evidence.title: Australian Frontier Wars: Hawkesbury (1794), Black War (1824), Pinjarra (1834) & Qld NMP
evidence.summary: Across Hawkesbury/Appin, Tasmania's Midlands, Pinjarra, Myall Creek, and Queensland, Indigenous defenders confronted mounted police and settler militias.
evidence.limits: Archival silences require systematic landscape forensics.

evidence.title: Raukkan, Poonindie, New Norcia & Ramahyuck (1847–1900): Aboriginal settlements
evidence.summary: Aboriginal residents rebuilt farming, craft, sporting, and educational communities across reserve and mission settlements while enduring colonial protections legislation.
evidence.limits: Recordkeeping mirrors missionary bias alongside family resilience.

evidence.title: Bismarck Archipelago (New Ireland & New Britain, PNG): 42 ka to Lapita stilt villages
evidence.summary: Pleistocene pelagic shellfish/obsidians at Matenkupkum followed by Makekur stilt villages and Watom pigs anchors Near Oceania chronology.
evidence.limits: Volcanic Rabaul and Witori tephras punctuate island sequences.

evidence.title: North Coast & East Sepik (Lachitu & Auwim, PNG): 6.8 ka fisheries & interior rock art
evidence.summary: Pre-Lapita coastal bone fishing tools and Upper Karawari painted caves document deep indigenous coastal–highland exchange on mainland New Guinea.
evidence.limits: Rainforest humidity narrows early organic preservation.

evidence.title: Caution Bay, Emo & Motupore (South Papua): 2,900 BP Lapita to Hiri pottery villages
evidence.summary: Mainland southern New Guinea preserves early Lapita arrival, ceramic transformation into Early Papuan Pottery, and historic Motu Hiri *lagatoi* towns.
evidence.limits: Delta alluviation buries submerged older horizons.

evidence.title: Gebe & Raja Ampat Passage (33–6 ka): Eastern Wallacean shell adzes & cuscus transport
evidence.summary: Direct maritime translocation of marsupials and obsidian along the Moluccas–Bird's Head corridor well before Neolithic voyagers.
evidence.limits: Small island trench sampling leaves many reefs unexcavated.

evidence.title: Guam/Tinian Latte, Babeldaob Hills & Yap *Rai* (Western Micronesia, 1500 BCE–1900)
evidence.summary: Direct ocean crossing at ~1500 BCE led to Latte limestone villages, Babeldaob monument earthworks, and Palau–Yap stone money (*rai*) fleets.
evidence.limits: Early Spanish colonial impact devastated Marianas outer populations.

evidence.title: Samoa Pulemelei, Tataga-Matau & Futuna (West Polynesia): Monumental chiefdoms
evidence.summary: Monolithic volcanic star mounds, Tutuila adze quarries, and irrigated Futuna valleys mark West Polynesia's chiefdom transformation.
evidence.limits: Inland forested slopes remain only selectively LiDAR-mapped.

evidence.title: Wairau Bar, Raoul Island (Kermadecs) & Wairau Affray: Two-way voyages to colonial clash
evidence.summary: Kermadec stepping stones confirm two-way East Polynesia–Aotearoa voyaging before distinct Māori regional settlements and 1843–1872 Crown wars.
evidence.limits: Intermittent Kermadec staging left thin volcanic tephra deposits.

evidence.title: Tetiʻaroa Atoll, Eiao Quarry & Austral/Cook Links (1100–1600): Central Polynesia stone sphere
evidence.summary: Every volcanic stone adze on coral Tetiʻaroa was carried by voyaging canoe from Tahiti, Raʻiatea, Eiao (Marquesas), or Rurutu.
evidence.limits: Post-16th-century shifts curbed multi-archipelago basalt transfers.

evidence.title: Mauna Kea, Hālawa & Kīholo (Hawaiʻi): Adze peaks, pondfields & marine sustainability
evidence.summary: Sub-alpine adze workshops at 3,780 m fed statewide Hawaiian exchange alongside walled *loko iʻa* fishponds and valley *heiau*.
evidence.limits: Volcanic flows and sugar agriculture reshaped ancient leeward tracts.

evidence.title: Rapa Nui *Moai*, *Ahu*, Freshwater Springs & Resilience (1200–1900)
evidence.summary: Rock-mulched sweet potato gardens anchored near coastal freshwater springs sustained cooperative Rapa Nui statue workshops prior to 1862 blackbirding.
evidence.limits: Debate over pre-contact ecological tipping vs post-contact devastation remains active.

waves.title: Georgina–Cooper Creek Pituri & Ochre Corridor
waves.summary: Continental desert trade network linking Mulligan pituri groves, Channel Country villages, and Flinders Ranges red ochre mines.
waves.limits: Ethnographic scale extrapolated onto late Holocene stone village hubs.

waves.title: Wilgie Mia Ochre & Kimberley Pearl-Shell Desert Network
waves.summary: Western Australian ochre quarries and coastal pearl/baler shell traveling >1,500 km across desert Songlines.
waves.limits: Radiocarbon dates show pre-colonial antiquity of desert shell transport (~2,000 BP).

waves.title: Wil-im-ee Moor-ring (Mount William) Greenstone Exchange
waves.summary: Kulin greenstone hatchet heads passing across 700 km of Murray–Darling and South Australian kinship exchanges.
waves.limits: Line schematics omit intermediate clan meeting sites.

waves.title: Arnhem Land – Makassar Monsoon *Trepang* Trade
waves.summary: Annual Macassan perahu voyages across the Banda and Arafura Seas exchanging iron, glass, and ceramics with Yolŋu trepangers.
waves.limits: Some Arnhem and Kimberley sites hint at occasional earlier pre-1650 SE Asian contacts.

waves.title: Torres Strait – Fly River – Cape York Exchange
waves.summary: Cross-strait canoe, shell, drum, and ochre exchange linking mainland Papua with Queensland.
waves.limits: Pre-European antiquity evidenced by ceramic and shell horizons on Dauar and Mabuyag.

waves.title: Bismarck Obsidian Sea Lanes (Talasea & Lou → Vanuatu & Fiji)
waves.summary: Geochemically fingerprinted New Britain and Admiralty obsidian carrying across 3,500 km of Lapita and post-Lapita reefs.
waves.limits: Frequency fell sharply outside the Bismarcks after ~600 BCE.

waves.title: Papuan Gulf Hiri, Vitiaz Strait & Massim *Kula* Networks
waves.summary: Interlocking coastal pottery, sago, shell-valuable (*Kula*), and obsidian sea circuits framing New Guinea.
waves.limits: Ethnographic Kula rings represent the last 500–600 years of older Massim links.

waves.title: Palau–Yap *Rai* Stone Money & Carolinian *Sawei* Corridor
waves.summary: Aragonite stone money quarried in Palau hauled to Yap, anchoring the hereditary *sawei* canoe network spanning Caroline atolls.
waves.limits: Late 19th-century foreign schooners altered cargo capacity.

waves.title: West Polynesian Basalt Adze & Fine-Mat Exchange (Samoa ↔ Tonga ↔ Fiji)
waves.summary: Tataga-Matau Samoan basalt adzes excavated at Lapaha confirm organized maritime prestige exchange.
waves.limits: Crossing antimeridian vectors connect Samoa-Tonga directly with Fiji across 180°.

waves.title: Eiao Basalt & Central-East Polynesian Interaction Sphere (>2,400 km)
waves.summary: XRF basalt sourcing ties Eiao (Marquesas) adzes across Tuamotus, Societies, and Cook Islands.
waves.limits: Inter-archipelago stone exchange waned after c. 1500 CE.

waves.title: Aotearoa *Tūhua* Obsidian & *Pounamu* Network (Kermadecs → Otago)
waves.summary: Mayor Island obsidian carried south alongside alpine West Coast nephrite jade (*pounamu*) north throughout Aotearoa and to Raoul Island.
waves.limits: Colonial musket trade shifted regional prestige networks after 1810.

waves.title: Hawaiian Inter-Island Adze Quarry Network (Mauna Kea → Oʻahu & Kauaʻi)
waves.summary: High-elevation Mauna Kea adzes, Molokaʻi blades, and Oʻahu quarries distributed across Hawaiian chiefdoms.
waves.limits: Late elite control increased redistribution specialization.

waves.title: Eastern & Interior Australian Frontier Wars (Hawkesbury–Myall–Qld, 1794–1900)
waves.summary: Generalized campaign zones tracing Darug, Wiradjuri, Gomeroi, Mithaka, and Kalkadoon armed defense against colonial frontier expansion.
waves.limits: Represents shifting frontier regions, not a single unified army.

waves.title: Lutruwita / Tasmania Black War & Black Line Operations (1824–1832)
waves.summary: Armed Palawa guerrilla defense across Tasmania's Settled Districts culminating in martial law, the 1830 Black Line, and Flinders Island exile.
waves.limits: Camps shifted continuously to evade military cordons.

waves.title: Tuʻi Tonga Expansion & Roviana *Tomoko* Raiding Spheres
waves.summary: Monumental Tongan earth forts and regional tribute traditions projecting maritime political influence across West Polynesia.
waves.limits: Direct military occupation vs marriage-tribute alliance varied across islands.

waves.title: Aotearoa Musket Wars & New Zealand Wars (1807–1872)
waves.summary: Major inter-tribal musket expeditions (1807–1837) followed by Northern, Taranaki, and Waikato *pā* campaigns against British imperial forces.
waves.limits: Trajectories compress dozens of distinct *iwi* campaigns.

waves.title: Hawaiian Kingdom Unification Campaigns (1782–1810)
waves.summary: Kamehameha I's war-canoe fleets and musket-supported campaigns uniting Hawaiʻi Island, Maui, Oʻahu (Nuʻuanu Pali 1795), and peace treaty with Kauaʻi (1810).
waves.limits: Kauaʻi joined via diplomacy rather than direct invasion.

waves.title: Dual Northern & Southern Maritime Routes into Pleistocene Sahul (65–45 ka)
waves.summary: Least-cost oceanographic dispersal pathways tracing Borneo–Sulawesi–Raja Ampat and Sunda–Timor–Kimberley crossings down through arid interior Australia and Tasmania.
waves.limits: Submerged Pleistocene shelves prevent mapping exact embarkation beaches.

waves.title: Western Micronesia (1500 BCE) & Lapita–West Polynesia Sea Dispersals (1200–850 BCE)
waves.summary: Independent Philippine–Mariana crossings and Bismarck–Vanuatu–Fiji–Tonga Lapita outrigger leapfrogs.
waves.limits: Later genetic admixture in Remote Melanesia modified ancestral populations.

waves.title: Polynesian Triangle Two-Way Expansion (Societies → Hawaiʻi, Rapa Nui & Aotearoa)
waves.summary: Explosive windward double-hulled canoe settlement reaching the Marquesas, Hawaiʻi, Rapa Nui, and Aotearoa/Kermadecs within three centuries.
waves.limits: Exact departure sequence across central atolls remains calibrated within decadal radiocarbon bounds.

waves.title: Kalkadoon Metabasalt, Pilbara Chert & Northern Leilira Stone Networks
waves.summary: Stone procurement corridors across the Pilbara, Ashburton Range (*leilira* blades), and Selwyn Range metabasalt axe quarries.
waves.limits: Petrographic and trace-element matching continues across scattered surface collections.

waves.title: Mangareva–Pitcairn–Henderson Polynesian Stone & Shell Sphere
waves.summary: Basalt adzes, volcanic glass, and pearl shell crossing hundreds of kilometres between fertile Mangareva and Pitcairn/Henderson until c. 1500 CE.
waves.limits: Abandoned outlying Pitcairn/Henderson settlements once return voyages stalled.

waves.title: Eastern Micronesia Megalithic Basalt & Coral Logistics (Pohnpei & Kosrae)
waves.summary: Rafted columnar basalt boulders from inland quarries around Pohnpei and Kosrae forming ceremonial seawalled compounds.
waves.limits: Line generalizes intra-island and regional Eastern Micronesian elite ties.

waves.title: Western, Southern & Kimberley Frontier Resistance (1834–1897)
waves.summary: Regional defense zones across SW Nyungar Pinjarra (1834), Lower Murray Overland Corner / Rufus River (1841), and Bunuba Kimberley gorges (1894–1897).
waves.limits: Represents disparate sovereign Aboriginal defense episodes.

waves.title: Sahul Denisovan Introgression & Remote Oceania Papuan–Austronesian Admixture
waves.dateLabel: c. 55 ka Denisovan gene flow; c. 500 BCE–500 CE Near–Remote Oceania admixture
waves.summary: Genomic arcs tracking ancient Denisovan alleles in Sahul populations and later post-Lapita Papuan ancestry expansion into Vanuatu and Fiji.
waves.limits: Schematic vector reflects genomic signals rather than continuous migration routes.
